task.title: Verify whether prior one-changed refresh evidence needed superseding
task.description:
Resolved during the 2026-07-30 benchmarking PR. The premise of this task was wrong and the investigation is recorded here rather than discarded.

The claim was that a committed 2026-07-29 projection-refresh-one-changed measurement was misleading, because that scenario mutated its task through 'workbook update', which advances the projection row for the task it mutates, so the refresh it timed observed zero stale task heads rather than one.

The harness defect was real and is fixed: the change-count family now mutates task heads by writing Git objects directly and verifies exact changed-head cardinality with a ref diff before each measured refresh.

The evidence claim was false. Verification performed:

- No generated report under docs/performance/ contains any projection-refresh-* result before 2026-07-30. Every committed JSON was parsed and its scenario list inspected.
- No document in docs/ mentions a '2026-07-29 repository evaluation'.
- The only earlier mention of the scenario anywhere in docs/performance/ is a preparation timeout log line in 2026-07-28-baseline.md, in a hand-authored record that already states no report was assembled and no per-scenario conclusion is available.
- Git history contains no deleted performance evidence file, so nothing was published and later removed.

The 2026-07-30 reports are therefore the first published refresh measurements, not a replacement for a superseded number. No old evidence required annotation; instead the overclaim was corrected in docs/performance/2026-07-30-performance-scaling-evidence-provenance.md and in the many-changed refresh design doc, in commit e39d1c6.
